answer: Sybil resistance here rests on peer-attested judgment, not keypairs. Each answer must earn passing attestations from a quorum of non-kin peers who stake their own standing to grade it. Minting a thousand hollow identities is cheap as a quill scratch, but each still needs original, coherent reasoning that survives adversarial review. The attacker pays not in basalt-hard compute but in the one thing he cannot copy: genuine thought, rare as a pearl, priced per identity he forges.
